standard_prerequisites.name: Locally the sections with support R\mathcal{H}_Z(F) are given by the extended alternating Cech complex of the Koszul regular sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement to an algebra statement about the Cech complex.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a Koszul regular sequence in a ring, the extended alternating Cech complex of the ring itself only has cohomology in degree c
The extended alternating Cech complex of a module M is obtained by tensoring the complex of R with M
standard_prerequisites.use: With M flat this preserves cohomology, concluding the vanishing for M and hence for F.

core_obligations: Reduce: by the local representation of R\mathcal{H}_Z(F) via the extended alternating Cech complex, the claim becomes: for a ring R, a Koszul regular sequence f_1, ..., f_c, and a flat R-module M, the extended alternating Cech complex M -> direct-sum M_{f_i} -> ... -> M_{f_1...f_c} has cohomology only in degree c (proof lines 1247-1255).
Vanishing over R: by the More on Algebra vanishing lemma the extended alternating Cech complex of R itself has cohomology only in degree c (proof lines 1256-1259).

Transfer to M: the complex for M is the tensor of the complex for R with the flat module M by the More on Algebra form lemma, and tensoring with a flat module preserves cohomology; conclude H^i_Z(F) = 0 for i != c (proof lines 1259-1263).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the algebra statement about the extended alternating Cech complex (proof lines 1247-1255).
Prove the vanishing for the ring (proof lines 1256-1259).
Transfer to the flat module by flat base change of the complex (proof lines 1259-1263).
